title: A Lean and Spec-Driven AI-Assisted Software Development Lifecycle for Applied AI Education: The AI-SDLC Approach
key_points: The paper proposes AI-SDLC, a lightweight six-phase lifecycle (Bootstrap, Specify, Design, Develop, Validate, Deploy) for governed AI-assisted software development, using AGENTS.md, SKILL.md files, specifications, and task documents as repository-local guidance.

AI-SDLC was applied in the FHNW course AI-assisted Software Development, and a descriptive cross-sectional survey of 13 students (from 34 invited) rated it positively, especially for structuring work and clarifying requirements.
Repository-local instruction files were judged helpful, but respondents' free-text accounts showed they sometimes failed, grew too large, or required ongoing maintenance.

Respondents reported confidence in generated code but low ability to follow it at any time; 11 of 13 described adopting code without fully understanding it, and verification relied more on running the software than on tests or pull requests.
Limitations include a small single-cohort sample, self-reported perceptions rather than observed outcomes, and little prior software engineering experience among respondents.
